intended_object: The center of a (possibly non-associative) ring R, viewed as a subring. Inferred from the docstring and the name. For associative rings it is the set {z | z·x = x·z for all x}.
explanation: The definition takes the carrier `Set.center R`, which consists of the elements satisfying `IsMulCentral`. It reuses the subsemiring structure from `Subsemiring.center` and adds closure under negation (`Set.neg_mem_center`). For an associative ring, `Set.center` is exactly the set of elements that commute with everything (`Semigroup.mem_center_iff`), as the docstring says. For a non-associative ring, `IsMulCentral` also asks that the element associate with all pairs of elements. This is the standard definition of the center of a non-associative ring (the commutative part of the nucleus), and the extra conditions are what make the center closed under multiplication. So the docstring's wording leaves out the associativity conditions, but the object defined is the right one. The setting, `NonAssocRing`, is the natural one for a subring: negation is needed for a subring, and associativity is not required. This is the standard Mathlib definition, so I judge it faithful.
